extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers, and users evaluating browser extensions for spotting altered or misleading images
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging browser extensions that detect altered or misleading images (functionality, effectiveness, privacy, trust, and deployment). Useful for assessing SurfSafe-style tools and similar image-authenticity plugins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose / claimed functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension is intended to help viewers spot fake news in the form of altered or misleadingly used images by comparing images in the browser to a database and informing the reader if an image has been altered or used misleadingly elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the extension actually implements the claimed functionality: does it compare images against a database of known images, and does it inform users when images are altered or used misleadingly? Example: SurfSafe places a check mark, a warning sign, or an X and can show the original image when identified as altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database coverage and sourcing (trusted sources list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works by comparing images to a database culled from a hundred trusted news or fact-checking sites (examples: Time, Snopes.com); users may also select their own group of websites besides Snopes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the breadth, quality, and curation of the source list. Danger: allowing users to choose sources can let less reliable outlets be included, blunting effectiveness and creating an echo chamber. Scoring should consider whether sources are vetted and how additions are controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image hashing / matching approach and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses a database of hashes of all images on every page any browser with the extension has visited and those hosted on the trusted-sites list; founders claimed rapid database growth if many users install the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the matching algorithm's resilience and the feasibility of scale claims (e.g., RoBhat's claim to accumulate huge numbers of images). Consider whether hashing handles transformations and how the system scales with user growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to image variants (crops, screenshots, different URLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests showed SurfSafe often failed to flag variants: it recognized some widely circulated copies but missed cropped versions, screenshots, or identical images on different pages with different URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key criterion is whether the tool recognizes altered variants (cropped, resized, screenshots, rehosted copies). Anti-pattern: marking only exact matches while missing common variants; deduct points for failure to detect variants in realistic viral circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text/context analysis linking image usage to pages
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension also analyzes any text on the page and compares it with text on pages where the image has appeared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the tool integrates textual context effectively (e.g., to detect misleading captions or reuse of images in different contexts) and whether text comparison improves or harms accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: User reporting and crowdsourcing mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can click a button if they believe a picture has been manipulated or misleadingly used, contributing to crowdsourced suspect-image reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the design and safeguards of crowdsourcing: how reports are validated, whether the system can be gamed, and whether crowdsourcing improves detection without enabling organized manipulation. Anti-pattern: relying on crowdsourcing without validation, enabling subversion by coordinated actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on viral circulation assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders argued that images the extension aims to spot spread virally, so if no other user has seen an image the extension cannot call it and will mark it as genuine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the danger of defaulting to 'genuine' when an image is unseen; consider prevalence of unique or engineered content and whether the approach penalizes novel manipulations. Systems should avoid false assurance for unseen images.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interface clarity and provenance display
rubrics_metrics.description: After comparisons, the extension places an icon at the corner: a check mark if genuine, a warning if suspect, and an X if identified elsewhere as altered; in the latter case it also shows the original image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge clarity, usefulness, and interpretability of UI signals. Good practice: show provenance and the original image when available. Watch for oversimplified indicators that may mislead users without context or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform availability and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Initially available only for Google Chrome and Opera; not available for any mobile platform at release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether target platforms match user behavior (desktop vs mobile). Limited platform availability reduces reach and usefulness, especially given many users access news primarily via mobile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on users' digital literacy and adoption barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics noted the underlying problem is digital literacy; expecting users whose main window is Facebook to install an add‑on is a leap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the tool requires actions or technical awareness that typical users won't perform. A solution overly reliant on voluntary installs or user initiative will have limited real-world impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability to echo chambers and trust-selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing users to choose trusted sites could lead to circles of trust that include outlets accused of propagating fake news, potentially blunting effectiveness or creating an echo chamber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mechanisms preventing self-reinforcing trust bubbles (e.g., default vetted lists, transparency about source reliability). Penalize designs that make it easy for users to create biased source sets without warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical performance / accuracy on real-world test cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent tests (e.g., The Verge) found SurfSafe came up short on widely circulated altered images and failed to flag important variants; prior project (BotCheck) claimed 93.5% accuracy on bot detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement: subject tools to independent, varied test sets including manipulated images, variants, and real-world viral cases. Score based on demonstrated recall/precision for identifying altered or misleading uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and data-collection practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Developer tools revealed the extension was querying the browser for the URL and all images on every page visited, sending them to RoBhat's servers; this could include private images and URLs with embedded credentials or tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy is a decisive criterion: evaluate what data is collected, whether sensitive URLs/tokens are transmitted, whether credentials are stripped, data retention, and opt-in/consent. Anti-pattern: collecting broad page/image data without clear disclosure or safeguards. Penalize products that expose private data or create attack surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and organizational trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations found the domain registration and site offered little information about RoBhat Labs or people involved; lack of 'About Us' raised trust issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess transparency of company identity, team, governance, and contactability. Trustworthy projects disclose personnel, policies, governance, data practices, and sources. Opaque organizations should be scored lower on trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security implications of implementation (tokens, URLs, scraping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because queries could include URLs with embedded credentials or tokens, even HTTPS would not prevent them from being passed along; while SurfSafe appeared to strip credentials when displaying publicly, that could break links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical security: are URL/query payloads sanitized, are credentials/exposed tokens protected, and does the extension introduce additional leakage risks? Implementation should avoid transmitting sensitive data and should preserve link integrity when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to model/community-induced biases and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders stated they would update models if SurfSafe developed a community that elevated less reliable outlets; they argued users noticing conflicts would self-correct, but also acknowledged model limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policies for model updates, moderation of community effects, and safeguards against community-driven elevation of unreliable sources. Good practice: proactive monitoring, transparent update policies, and mechanisms to correct emergent biases.
